requirement:
The requirements index links to its documented-coverage-gaps subchapter
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index`.
rationale:
The obligation is that the requirements index links to its documented-coverage-gaps subchapter, which sits under the index. The parent `requirements.test-coverage.index` covers both explicitly placed and automatically generated indexes. I did not request implementation source. The three tests cover the obligation as follows.

- **Explicitly placed index:** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` uses an index chapter with a `{requirements-index}` directive at `appendix/requirements-index.md`.
  - It asserts the index content contains `[Documented coverage gaps](requirements-index/coverage.html)`. That path is correct relative to the index file.
  - It asserts exactly one `Documented coverage gaps` sub-chapter exists under the index, at `appendix/requirements-index/coverage.md`, with `parent_names` equal to `["Requirements index"]`.
- **Automatically generated index:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` builds a book with no index marker.
  - It asserts the default top-level index contains `[Documented coverage gaps](requirements-index/coverage.html)`.
  - It asserts exactly one coverage subchapter at `requirements-index/coverage.md` with the index as its parent.
- **Nested or placed index:** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` puts the index at `reports.md` under a parent section.
  - It asserts the index content contains `[Documented coverage gaps](reports/coverage.html)`.
  - It asserts the subchapter's path, parent names and section numbers.
  - It runs with numbered and unnumbered parents.

A wrong link target, a missing link or a misplaced subchapter would fail these assertions. All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no unaddressed obligation or marking gap.
